tagline: Cambodia's island riviera — fast-growing, going upmarket, and almost entirely untapped on the water.
summary: Sihanoukville is Cambodia's coastal gateway, and a short 12–15 nm hop across the Gulf of Thailand sits its island riviera: Koh Rong and Koh Rong Sanloem, where backpacker beaches now share the water with serious luxury (Song Saa, Six Senses Krabey, Alila Koh Russey, Royal Sands). Visitor numbers to the islands are climbing fast, yet barely 1% of Cambodia's tourists travel by water at all — the upside is enormous. Today's speedboats and fast ferries are cheap but monsoon-fragile and rough; smooth, reliable, zero-emission foiling turns the crossing itself into part of the destination.

use_cases.title: Reliable island crossing
use_cases.body: Replace the monsoon-fragile speedboat/fast-ferry on the Sihanoukville↔Koh Rong/Sanloem run (12–15 nm) with all-electric foiling — smooth, fast and far less prone to weather cancellation across the open Gulf of Thailand.

use_cases.title: Private resort transfers
use_cases.body: Direct, quiet foiling transfers to the luxury micro-cluster — Song Saa, Six Senses Krabey, Alila Koh Russey, Royal Sands — turning a bumpy speedboat transfer into a serene, zero-emission arrival.

use_cases.title: Coastal & cross-border reach
use_cases.body: Extend down the Ream National Park coast and out toward Koh Kong, with a long-range hybrid link to Vietnam's Phu Quoc — opening a Gulf-of-Thailand island circuit no operator runs today.

journeys.today: A 20–45 minute speedboat or fast ferry across open Gulf water — cheap but rough, and cancelled in the wet-season swell.
journeys.with_navier: An all-electric foiling crossing that flies above the chop — smooth, quiet and weather-resilient, so the schedule actually holds.

journeys.today: A separate speedboat transfer, pounding across the swell to private resort jetties.
journeys.with_navier: A wake-light foiling arrival straight to the resort jetty — the transfer becomes part of the luxury experience, not the worst part of the trip.

journeys.today: No direct sea link — travellers backtrack to the mainland and fly or bus the long way round.
journeys.with_navier: A long-range hybrid passage opens a direct Gulf-of-Thailand island-to-island crossing, stitching Cambodia's and Vietnam's island resorts into one circuit.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The core crossings are comfortably in all-electric range: Sihanoukville↔Koh Rong (~13 nm) and ↔Koh Rong Sanloem (~15 nm), plus the short inter-island and Ream-coast hops. This is the high-frequency, volume-carrying network — and the leg that most rewards foiling's smoother, more weather-resilient ride.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The Koh Rong↔Phu Quoc cross-border link (~55 nm, near the all-electric range edge and worth a coordinate check before it becomes a marquee routed leg) and the longer reach toward Koh Kong suit the long-range hybrid, which carries the crossing without island-end charging and gives schedule margin across an exposed open-water leg.

competitive_landscape: The islands are served today by a handful of conventional fast-ferry and speedboat operators (Speed Ferry Cambodia, Buva Sea and others) — five-plus services on short, cheap runs. They are frequent but rough, diesel-powered and weather-fragile, cancelling in monsoon swell. With island visitation climbing fast and water-transport penetration near zero nationwide, the demand is proven and the on-water experience is wide open for a clean, comfortable, reliable upgrade.
seasonality: The southwest monsoon (May–Oct) brings the rough season to the Gulf of Thailand — wind, swell and the speedboat cancellations that strand island travellers — while Nov–Apr is the calm peak. There is no typhoon track this far west. Monsoon weather-fragility is the single strongest demand hook here: foiling flies above the chop that grounds conventional fast-craft, converting cancellation risk into a reliability premium.
regulatory_note: Operations run through the Sihanoukville Autonomous Port and the Ministry of Public Works & Transport, with Ream National Park (Ministry of Environment) adjacent — a born-protected coastline that gives a clean, zero-emission fleet a conservation rationale. A cross-border Phu Quoc link would require Cambodia–Vietnam maritime and immigration coordination at designated terminals.
signature_routes: Sihanoukville ↔ Koh Rong Sanloem (luxury resort transfers)
Koh Rong ↔ Phu Quoc (cross-border Gulf-of-Thailand island circuit)

precedents.what: ~100-vessel, $100M phased clean-marine network with JIH Global, first 5 vessels in 2026
precedents.why_it_matters: Shows resort-island transfers and inter-island crossings built into a clean-marine network at scale — the model for Cambodia's emerging luxury island cluster.

deck_only.commercial_framing: Cleanest entry is the luxury micro-cluster (Song Saa / Six Senses / Alila / Royal Sands) as a premium-transfer anchor, with the Sihanoukville↔Koh Rong public crossing as the volume layer and Koh Rong↔Phu Quoc as the headline cross-border showcase. Near-zero waterway penetration nationally means almost all of the addressable transfer demand is greenfield.
deck_only.platform_split_rationale: All-electric carries the in-range island crossings (the volume); long-range hybrid is reserved for the ~55 nm cross-border Phu Quoc link and longer Koh Kong reach. Flag the Phu Quoc distance as near the all-electric range edge pending a coordinate check.

internal.convener_notes: A Cambodia mandate via the Sampriti network is upcoming, and Taj Hotels' Cambodia presence offers a rare warm hospitality anchor for SEA — both are the preferred entry channels here. Royal Group (Sokimex) is the Royal Sands Koh Rong developer and a likely state-adjacent counterparty. Treat the recent Sihanoukville casino-driven boom/bust and Chinese-investment sensitivities as context, not pitch material. Cross-link: Phu Quoc (Vietnam) is the cross-border sister node — wire the map edge once both briefs are live.
